correctness.rationale: Fresh check of the corrected RESULT.md: L¹-small kernel truncation gives norm approximation by Hilbert–Schmidt operators for every α>0, not just above α=1/2. Reflection exchanges J_α and its adjoint and hence anticommutes with the compact self-adjoint defect. On the separated rectangle the right-end integral has an ordinary convergent Taylor series; substituting t=xu in the left-end integral gives x^α times a convergent analytic series with coefficients (−1)^k binom(α−1,k) B(k+1,α)y^(α−1−k). For noninteger α none of those scalar factors vanishes. A nonzero analytic germ and x^α times a nonzero analytic germ have distinct leading exponents; this isolates the fractional coefficients even for α below 1. Vandermonde independence then holds for every finite set of distinct test columns (for y=1/3,1/2,2/3 the determinant in the reciprocals is −3/4). The compressed operator's columns are limits in L² of averaged outputs, so finite rank would force all columns into its closed finite-dimensional range. This proves infinite rank, and compactness plus pairing proves infinite inertia of each sign. The corrected integer comparison explicitly restricts the polynomial assertion to eigenfunctions for nonzero eigenvalues. The factorial sign follows by grouping ± pairs, and for m=1 the independent coefficient/Gram calculation gives −1/12. The original checker was inspected, not executed; its exact finite tests are consistency checks, with replay instructions in the corrected files.
